official_source.title: Operations and Readiness Records
official_source.current_nara_notice: Some items superseded or obsolete; remaining active items listed by NARA as of 2024-11-04. Most other items were later superseded by DAA-NU-2015-0003.

material_findings.relevance: Directly demonstrates that an operational combat-information-center log class in the older Navy schedule was temporary rather than permanent.

material_findings.record_class: Flight/squadron scheduling and adjacent operational records
material_findings.historical_disposition_text: Several classes had retention measured in months to a few years.
material_findings.relevance: Shows that exercise/flight operational context records could expire long before modern UAP requests.

material_findings.historical_disposition_text: The schedule contains temporary general/operational categories with retention commonly measured in roughly one to three years, while selected primary program records were permanent.
material_findings.relevance: Demonstrates differential retention inside electronic-warfare record families; not every EW-related record was permanent.

critical_limit: R4 DOES NOT ESTABLISH THAT USS PRINCETON AN/SPY-1 RAW TARGET RETURNS, AEGIS ELECTRONIC WAR DIARY DATA, E-2C TRACKS, OR AIR-DEFENSE AUDIO WERE CLASSIFIED UNDER ANY OF THESE SPECIFIC N1-NU-89-005 ITEMS IN NOVEMBER 2004. The exact 2004 record class and applicable disposition authority remain to be resolved.
relationship_to_2010_schedule: N1-NU-10-003 later created SSIC 3101 specifically for electronic/digital shipboard operations monitoring and stated that existing SSICs did not address retention of those record types. Therefore the older schedule proves short-lived adjacent operational classes existed, while the 2010 schedule proves a later need for a dedicated electronic-monitoring category.

pattern_effect.reason: The retention mechanism is no longer supported only by a post-event 2010 schedule; a pre-2010 Navy operations/readiness schedule independently shows temporary CIC/EW/flight operational record classes. Exact 2004 SPY-1 applicability remains unresolved.

next_exact_question: Which SSIC / records schedule item governed USS Princeton CG-59 AN/SPY-1/Aegis track data, CIC tactical logs, and exercise-monitoring recordings on 14 November 2004, and is there a disposition/transfer record for those data?
canonical_seal: SHORT RETENTION EXISTED IN THE RIGHT NAVY OPERATIONS NEIGHBORHOOD BEFORE 2010. THAT EXPLAINS HOW DATA COULD VANISH; IT DOES NOT YET PROVE WHICH RULE GOVERNED THE PRINCETON DATA.
